title: A Locker for the Yearbook
premise: Freya Okonkwo just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built over the ruins of a shuttered reform school whose records were never unsealed. When her history teacher pairs her with Theo Vance — the golden boy whose family helped bury those records — for a semester project on local history, they unearth a locker from the old school containing a dead student's diary and proof of a decades-old cover-up. As Freya falls for Theo against every instinct of loyalty to the victims' families she's secretly connected to, she must choose between exposing the truth at the state championship his future depends on or protecting the boy who chose her over his name. In the end, Freya publishes the diary during the final audition he was counting on — and discovers Theo had already decided to burn his own scholarship speech to read the victim's name aloud instead.
about_author: Petra Marchetti is a former archivist who spent three years cataloguing sealed institutional records before turning to fiction. She writes young adult novels about ordinary teenagers who refuse to let buried things stay buried.

chapters.title: Head Down, Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. New in town, Freya has one rule: stay invisible. But her history teacher assigns a semester project pairing her with Theo Vance, the school's untouchable golden boy, on 'Hollow Creek: A Century of Progress.' Researching in the basement archives, Freya finds a floor plan showing a wing that officially never existed. The emotional beat is wary curiosity curdling into unease as she realizes the school's foundation sits on erased lives.

chapters.title: The Combination
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya and Theo POV. Forced together by the project, the rivals trace the missing wing to a 1971 fire and discover a rusted locker pried from the rubble, stashed in a maintenance tunnel. Inside: a diary belonging to Marcus Bell, a student who died the night of the fire — and evidence the blaze was set to destroy abuse records. The beat is reluctant alliance deepening into trust, then attraction neither will name.

chapters.title: What the Trophy Case Hides
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo recognizes his grandfather's signature on the cover-up documents and spirals: expose it and lose everything — scholarship, family, identity — or stay silent and become complicit. Meanwhile Freya learns her own aunt survived the reform school and has waited fifty years for someone to listen. With the championship and the final audition looming, Theo must decide which version of himself to be. The beat is love colliding with duty.

chapters.title: Read the Name Aloud
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax to resolution. At the state championship, Freya publishes Marcus Bell's diary online mid-game; the gym goes silent as phones light up. Instead of delivering his rehearsed audition speech, Theo walks to the podium and reads the names of the forgotten students while his family watches. The old wing is memorialized, the records unsealed, and Freya — finally visible — opens her locker to find Theo's note inside. The beat is justice won together, love chosen freely.
